summary: Kanban EV is a dense, interlocking worker-placement/action-point game where you juggle multiple resource chains (car components, R&D, JIT contracts) across a tight board with heavy multi-use action spaces; turns are short but decisions are agonizing because every action interacts with several systems at once. It rewards efficient engine-building and planning several moves ahead more than direct confrontation with opponents.
praised: Tight, elegant interlocking systems where every action affects multiple resources
Streamlined and more approachable than the original Kanban: Automotive Revolution while keeping its depth
Satisfying puzzle of optimizing just-in-time production and R&D upgrades
High replayability due to multiple viable strategies
criticised: Steep learning curve and lengthy rules overhead for a new group
Feels iterative rather than groundbreaking to players who already own the original Kanban
Dry, spreadsheet-like theme integration despite the EV dressing
Long teach and setup time relative to actual play tension

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial on worker placement spaces, indirect competition for shared resources/contracts

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple independent systems (contracts fulfilled, R&D/technology tracks, department efficiency, end-game bonuses), so the winner is usually whoever balances several engines rather than maxing one.
